title: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 14](/bible/2-samuel/14)

## Introduction

Chapter 14 turns on David's longing for Absalom. Joab, perceiving the king's heart, sends a wise woman of Tekoah to speak a parable that traps David into recalling his own banished son. David discerns Joab's hand in it, yet still grants the request and brings Absalom back to Jerusalem, though he refuses to see his face for two full years. The wisdom never departed from David even after his fall; he was still anointed of the Most High, still king over all Israel, and still a very wise man. Absalom's beauty and his weight of hair are noted, and his persistence in setting Joab's field on fire finally gets him back into the king's presence.

**[2 Samuel 14:1-3](/bible/2-samuel/14#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/14#v1)</sup> Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/14#v2)</sup> And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/14#v3)</sup> And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.

- Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom, and sent to Tekoah and fetched a wise woman, telling her to feign herself a mourner, put on mourning apparel, and speak to the king in the manner he taught her.
- Joab put the words in her mouth. He set up the whole scene to move the king toward bringing Absalom home.

**[2 Samuel 14:4-11](/bible/2-samuel/14#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/14#v4)</sup> And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/14#v5)</sup> And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I am indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/14#v6)</sup> And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/14#v7)</sup> And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband neither name nor remainder upon the earth.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/14#v8)</sup> And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/14#v9)</sup> And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house: and the king and his throne be guiltless.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/14#v10)</sup> And the king said, Whosoever saith ought unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/14#v11)</sup> Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the Lord thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.

- The woman of Tekoah told the king she was a widow whose two sons strove in the field, and one slew the other, and now the whole family rose up to kill the surviving son, seeking to quench her one remaining coal and leave her husband no name upon the earth. David swore that not one hair of her son would fall to the earth.
- Joab had her act as a widow, saying the revenger of blood was coming for her last son. She knew, as Joab knew, that David was merciful, so she framed it around the law of the revenger of blood to draw out his mercy.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 35:19](/bible/numbers/35#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/numbers/35#v19)</sup> The revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer: when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.

    The revenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer; when he meeteth him, he shall slay him.

**[2 Samuel 14:12-17](/bible/2-samuel/14#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/14#v12)</sup> Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak one word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/14#v13)</sup> And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/14#v14)</sup> For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/14#v15)</sup> Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/14#v16)</sup> For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/14#v17)</sup> Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the Lord thy God will be with thee.

- The woman then asked leave to speak one word, and turned it on David: why had he thought such a thing against the people of God, since by this judgment he condemned himself, in that he fetched not home his banished? We must needs die, as water spilt on the ground, yet God devises means that his banished be not expelled from him.
- She turned his own words against him: you told me to bring my son back and nothing would happen to him, but what about your own son? Even the Most High is not a respecter of persons and does not keep his banished banished forever, so she trapped him in his own situation.

**[2 Samuel 14:18-20](/bible/2-samuel/14#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/14#v18)</sup> Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/14#v19)</sup> And the king said, Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/14#v20)</sup> To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.

- The king asked the woman not to hide the thing he would ask: was not the hand of Joab with her in all this? She answered that none could turn to the right hand or the left from what the king had spoken; his servant Joab bade her, and put all these words in her mouth. Joab did this to fetch about this form of speech, and the king was wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God.
- David knew. As anointed and worthy as David was, and as wise, there was no way he did not know what kind of man his own right-hand man Joab was. Though David made a mistake, the wisdom never departed from him; David was always on point. This also answers those who use David's mistake to justify their sins; they do not know the Bible, for his house had incest, murder, and now this scheme, and David still saw through all of it.

**[2 Samuel 14:21-24](/bible/2-samuel/14#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/14#v21)</sup> And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/14#v22)</sup> And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, To day thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/14#v23)</sup> So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/2-samuel/14#v24)</sup> And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king’s face.

- The king told Joab he had done this thing, and commanded him to go bring the young man Absalom again. Joab fell on his face, thanked the king, and said he now knew he had found grace in the king's sight. Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem, but the king said, Let him turn to his own house and not see my face.
- Joab set the whole thing up to get Absalom back. David showed mercy by letting him return to Jerusalem, but said, Tell him not even to come see me; go to his own house.

**[2 Samuel 14:25-27](/bible/2-samuel/14#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/2-samuel/14#v25)</sup> But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-samuel/14#v26)</sup> And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year’s end that he polled it: because the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king’s weight.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-samuel/14#v27)</sup> And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.

- In all Israel there was none so praised as Absalom for his beauty; from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish. When he polled his head at every year's end, because the hair was heavy on him, he weighed the hair at two hundred shekels after the king's weight. Unto Absalom were born three sons and one daughter named Tamar, a woman of a fair countenance.
- Polled means to cut; people got haircuts back then. Two hundred shekels after the king's weight was heavy, for the king had pure everything, so that is a great deal of hair to grow back every year. Absalom named his daughter Tamar, which shows the respect he had for his sister.

**[2 Samuel 14:28-33](/bible/2-samuel/14#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/2-samuel/14#v28)</sup> So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king’s face.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-samuel/14#v29)</sup> Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-samuel/14#v30)</sup> Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/2-samuel/14#v31)</sup> Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/2-samuel/14#v32)</sup> And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it had been good for me to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/2-samuel/14#v33)</sup> So Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.

- Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem and saw not the king's face. He sent for Joab twice to send him to the king, but Joab would not come, so Absalom had his servants set Joab's barley field on fire. Then Joab came, and Absalom said, Let me see the king's face, and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me. Joab told the king, and Absalom came and bowed himself, and the king kissed Absalom.
- Absalom was trying to get the king's attention, and when Joab would not respond, he set the man's field on fire to force the matter. This was straight craziness, but it finally brought him before the king, and David kissed him.
